excerpt: Let C = <D exists> and D = <C exists>; D truthmakes C and C truthmakes D. Let E = <F is true> and F = <E is true>; the fact that E is true grounds the fact that F is true, and conversely.
overview: These paired constructions supply non-reflexive failures of asymmetry. They matter because asymmetry is not defeated only by self-grounding; the source also claims there can be distinct relata standing in grounding-like relations in both directions.
title: Mutual Proposition Grounding
